dispersion.interpretation: variance is fully consistent with chance - no evidence that any course is more popular than any other

uniformity.interpretation: cannot reject uniform allocation: the enrolment pattern is statistically indistinguishable from transactions assigned to courses at random

EnrollmentCount.interpretation: no attribute is associated with EnrollmentCount once corrected for testing 17 hypotheses

CourseRevenue.interpretation: 7 attribute(s) associated with CourseRevenue after correction: CoursePrice, PriceVsCategory, PricePerHour, CategoryMedianPrice, PriceXRating, CourseType, PriceBand

tautology.interpretation: revenue is arithmetically determined by price and enrolments, and a rule with no model at all reaches R² = 0.9932. Any learned model must be scored against this, not against the mean.

verdict.summary: NO DEMAND SIGNAL. Enrolment counts are consistent with random allocation, and no course attribute predicts them after correcting for multiple testing. Any positive R² a model reports for enrolment on this data is fitted noise.
